{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   -N 1
#   -n 24
#   -t 0-06:00:00
#   -q normal
#   -o slurm.%j.out
#   -e slurm.%j.err
#   --mail-type=ALL
#   --mail-user=%u@asu.edu
#   --export=NONE

#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 24
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=6h

# Omitted Slurm option: -q normal (QoS)
# Flux QoS/priority mappings are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may have different priority/limits than intended, affecting wait time or eligibility.

# Omitted Slurm options: -o/-e with %j token
# Slurm's %j token (job id) is not portable in Flux output/error directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames.

# Omitted Slurm options: --mail-type and --mail-user
# Flux does not provide a universal, built-in email notification directive in batch scripts.
# Performance implication: none on runtime performance, but you will not receive automatic job emails.

# Omitted Slurm option: --export=NONE
# Flux does not have a portable directive identical to Slurm --export=NONE.
# Performance implication: a larger inherited environment may change tool behavior (e.g., compilers, proxies, paths) and affect reproducibility.

module purge

curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh

source "$HOME/.cargo/env"

# Slurm did not use srun; to use allocated tasks under Flux, launch with flux-run.
# If this is a single-process build/run, requesting -n 24 may waste resources.
flux run -n 1 cargo run
"
}
